audit.whatIsWrong: diffRating and carryRating were empty strings while breakdown.difficulty and report[14] both state 6/10 and 6/10.
audit.why: Blank rating fields render an empty badge against prose that already gives the numbers. Enum fields, exempt from the length band.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four of seven side tokens contradicted their own why-lines. win[0]/phases[0].side said 'Dr. Mundo' above whys[0] 'Yone's Q knockup buildup and mixed damage out-poke you at Level 1'; win[1] said 'Skill' above a Yone-favoured why; win[4] said 'Dr. Mundo' above whys[4] 'Level 6 favours Yone'; win[6] said 'Yone' above whys[6] 'your full HP stacks and Q sustain finally out-endure his burst'.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is [Yone x6, Dr. Mundo] with no defects flagged, and it matches whys[] on every disputed row. At 49.08% over 2981 games this is a lane Dr. Mundo loses until he is fully stacked — the tokens had scattered three fake Dr. Mundo windows through the early game, including at Level 1 where his own why-text says the opposite.
audit.corrected: Four flips as one atomic group across both layers, plus phases[4].why and phases[5].why which asserted the opposite of their corrected side.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text describes Fate Sealed as 'a wide dash-knockup'. It is not a knockup. Separately, Spirit Cleave (W) is absent from the entire page.
audit.why: Riot's text: Yone 'blinks behind the last champion in a line with a slash so powerful it pulls all enemies hit towards him.' That is a blink-and-pull — it drags you back through his team, the opposite of being knocked away, and the kit carries no knockup flag on R (the knockup is Mortal Steel's Q3). Spirit Cleave meanwhile shields him on a 14s base cooldown that shortens with attack speed, and the shield grows with champions hit — that is the burst absorber sitting between your Heart Zapper and his health bar, and nothing on the page mentioned it.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text now states the blink-and-pull; report[5].t and breakdown.cooldowns now carry Spirit Cleave's shield and 14s base.

audit.whatIsWrong: Soul Unbound was listed as a flat 22s.
audit.why: It is 22/19/16/13/10. Maxed it is 10 seconds — a fifth of a minute between free, consequence-free trade windows, not the 22s the page implies. Fate Sealed is likewise 120/100/80, not stated anywhere.
audit.corrected: 22s at rank 1 / 10s maxed in both the cooldown block and report[5]; R's 120s rank 1 added to spikes[1].

edits.before: Maximum Dosage online — dives and all-ins flip when you press R mid-fight and regen half your HP. Force Yone to commit, then out-last the commit.
edits.after: Fate Sealed blinks behind you and drags you back in, setting up his whole combo. Maximum Dosage heals part of it, not all — never duel him at 6 alone.

edits.before: Heartsteel timing — every proc widens the HP gap and your cleavers start hurting. Stand in the wave and dare Yone to trade into the regen.
edits.after: His first crit item outpaces one Heartsteel, and Spirit Cleave shields him every 14s while Soul Unbound covers the exit. Farm the wave, don't duel.

edits.before: Yone R Fate Sealed is a wide dash-knockup that sets up his full burst, and his E means he can commit with a built-in escape. Your R Maximum Dosage heals a chunk, but his sustained mixed damage plus ignite can still outpace it in a solo all-in.
edits.after: Fate Sealed blinks him behind you and PULLS you toward him — it is a drag into his team, not a knockup, and it is 120s at rank 1. Your R heals a chunk, but his mixed damage plus ignite still outpaces it in a solo all-in.

edits.before: - Yone Soul Unbound (22s): matchup-defining — He snaps back when it ends. Chase him there. Track it before every commit. - Your ultimate: spend it on kill windows, never on waves. - Summoners: track his Flash after any close call — it changes every dive call.
edits.after: - Yone Soul Unbound (22s at rank 1, 10s maxed): he snaps back to his body when it ends — that spot is your window. - Spirit Cleave (14s base, faster with attack speed) shields him. - Your ultimate: kill windows only. - Track his Flash after a close call.

edits.before: Track Yone’s Soul Unbound (22s): He snaps back when it ends. Chase him there. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Soul Unbound is 22s at rank 1 but only 10s maxed — and Spirit Cleave shields him every 14s, so force that shield out first.

edits.before: Your windows: Level 6, First item, 2+ items. His windows: Level 1, Level 2. Fight at your spikes, concede his — the level chart above is the trade calendar.
edits.after: Your window: 2+ items, and that is the only one. His: Level 1 through first item. Fight at your spike, concede the rest — the chart above is the calendar.

edits.before: See the level-by-level chart — fight in your windows (Level 6, First item, 2+ items), respect his (Level 1, Level 2).
edits.after: See the level-by-level chart — your one window is 2+ items; respect everything from Level 1 through first item.

notes: Fate Sealed was described as a knockup. It is a blink-behind plus a PULL toward Yone — a player who spaces for a knockup gets dragged the wrong way into his team. Spirit Cleave did not appear anywhere on the page despite being the shield that eats Heart Zapper's burst on a 14s base cooldown. The chart also carried three fabricated Dr. Mundo windows (Levels 1, 2 and 6) directly above why-text stating Yone wins those levels.
